ActorTalk: Crimson Banner: The Age of Exodus
This work captures the soul of the Great Evacuation era.
In the painting, Constructs draped in crimson banners stand beside human soldiers. The banner is both a symbol of hope and a mark of sacrifice.

The worn textures in the background reflect the era itself—gray tones echo the ashes of Earth ravaged by Punishing, while scattered colors blend engine trails and the flickering lights of humanity's escape to Babylonia.
It records the most tragic moment of the Great Evacuation—the last stand, where Constructs and humans fought together to buy time for others to survive.
The rough brushstrokes feel like scars left by war. Within the clash of colors are two cries at once: a painful farewell to Earth, and a stubborn vow to keep civilization alive in Babylonia.
Every torn block of color reflects the cost of survival in the Great Evacuation era. We left Earth behind, but the direction the crimson banner points—toward Babylonia—proves that humanity endures.
